blocks.3: the Midtun farmers have used these hillsides,
blocks.4: at first for trapping and hunting;
blocks.5: many a quarry has surely been brought down here.
blocks.6: They used the juicy outfield grass;
blocks.7: the outfield mowing went on in earnest and in fun.
blocks.8: Here in summer cows heavy with milk swayed,
blocks.9: sheep and other animals ran in their masses.
blocks.10: Green and fine were the meadows,
blocks.11: birch adorned the hillsides and knolls;
blocks.12: it is strange to think back
blocks.13: that so much juniper should come here.
blocks.14: In older times there was teeming life with summer farming;
blocks.15: the dairymaids made cheese and churned, tended their herd.
blocks.16: Later the women came in the evening with containers and pails,
blocks.17: milked the herd and stayed the night in their summer-farm hut.
blocks.18: In the morning they milked once more
blocks.19: before trudging the long way home.
blocks.20: The container could be quite heavy,
blocks.21: but the girl was fit and young.
blocks.22: Together the women set off cheerfully along the path;
blocks.23: they knitted, chatted and enjoyed themselves.
blocks.24: They could not hurry along the path in one go,
blocks.25: no, at certain places they had their rests,
blocks.26: and there the chatter flowed extra easily,
blocks.27: the knitting grew from neat balls of yarn,
blocks.28: it all seemed so simple and easy,
blocks.29: and the "clog post" was never short of material.
blocks.30: Still, it was bound to be tiring,
blocks.32: with unsettled weather, rain and drizzle
blocks.33: and miserable wet in scrub and bush.
blocks.34: Then many a time they wished
blocks.35: there had been a road to drive on.
blocks.36: And even more often it was surely wished for
blocks.37: by the men who fetched wood in Dalen in winter.
blocks.38: If little snow came, with poor going in the outfields,
blocks.39: it could often put a strain on their temper.
blocks.40: As grazing in the valley came more and more to an end,
blocks.41: the forest grew with more and more vigour.
blocks.42: If we had got ourselves a road for a tractor,
blocks.43: the gain could surely have been great.
blocks.44: We could have drawn up a grand planting plan,
blocks.45: got the valley full of beautiful, valuable spruce.
blocks.46: So we thought as time went by,
blocks.47: but the farmers got a new spark,
blocks.48: and now, I must say, things went fast;
blocks.49: the public machinery ran as if oiled,
blocks.50: with planning, staking out, subsidies and everything;
blocks.51: surely nothing could go wrong now?
blocks.54: He set to work with his new digger;
blocks.55: both he and the machine could take a knock.
blocks.58: he was an excellent machine operator,
blocks.61: worked and sweated, thundered and blasted.
blocks.62: The farmers themselves went in for voluntary work,
blocks.63: threw themselves into it with zeal and pleasure,
blocks.64: were not afraid to wade in the mud,
blocks.65: drilled, laid pipes and hauled in fill.
blocks.66: The work went as if done by professionals,
blocks.67: and the road grew longer day by day;
blocks.68: it wound its way forward like a snake
blocks.69: and was tried and welcomed by many.
blocks.70: We saw a great difference from weekend to weekend;
blocks.72: and it did not last long either
blocks.73: before the result matched our hopes;
blocks.76: Now it lies here like a glittering thread,
blocks.78: winding along, level and on the slant,
blocks.79: good to drive a tractor on
blocks.81: the whole village will and must
blocks.82: come in to try it and see!
blocks.83: We are proud of you lads,
blocks.84: who over bogs, rocks and peaks
blocks.85: have made such a splendid road
blocks.86: at a price that will trouble no one.
blocks.87: We thank all who have shown their good side,
blocks.88: and sent help and subsidies for the project.
blocks.89: People of Midtun, congratulations on the road you have got!
blocks.90: We wish it may serve you long and well,
blocks.91: give you much joy and benefit,
blocks.92: and that you may truly enjoy it.
